title: Choose RELOOP AI's visual world
question: The roll assigned the Kabadiwala Rate Board. Keep it, take my pick, or re-roll.

options.label: Kabadiwala Rate Board
options.lineage: Neighbourhood raddiwala shops: hand-painted tin rate boards, carbon-copy weighing chits, rubber stamps
options.thesis: RELOOP AI as the neighbourhood kabadiwala, made honest and digital: every item gets weighed up, written on a chit and sent to the right place.
materials: enamel-painted signboard panels in forest green with white lettering
ruled carbon-copy chit with carbon-blue filled fields
options.viewport: A forest-green painted rate board takes the top of the page. RELOOP AI and the headline are lettered on it, and its rows list materials (wet, dry, e-waste, hazardous, textiles, reusable) with where each goes. A blank chit sits pinned to the board with a working 'Upload a waste photo' field and a 'Donate an item' action beside it.
options.risk: Sign-painter lettering turns kitschy if it's faked with a novelty font. It needs a sturdy grotesque cut like painted lettering, and white space kept sharp.

raised.raise: Nothing disappears, it gets stamped: Pending Review, Available, Reserved, Completed and Rejected stamp onto the listing's chit, so history stays readable.
State is shown by shape, not just colour: the AI's certainty level (clear, likely, unsure) is a filled, half or hollow mark, so it reads without colour vision.
Full traceability: every line on a result chit links back to the document it came from, or says 'no source loaded'.
One fixed safety strip: hazard warnings use one unmissable band that can't be dismissed, the same on every page.
The system writes its own state: the AI's checks are printed as lines on the chit ('Checked: hazard rules. No local guidance loaded.'), not hidden behind spinners.
Distinct states are kept: a rate-board row reads as active, unavailable or needs-review without relying on hover.

options.label: Municipal Bin Stencils
options.lineage: Municipal segregation bins and van signage: green wet, blue dry, red hazardous, stencilled lettering
options.thesis: The page is the segregation system itself: every item lands in a coloured lane with a stencilled label.
options.viewport: A row of large colour lanes with stencilled names fills the top. Above them, an upload field reads 'Which bin? Show us a photo.'
options.risk: This is the familiar answer for a waste product. It's very clear, but it's the direction most runs in this category end up with, and it leaves donation and reuse feeling secondary.

options.label: Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: Each item's journey from home to its destination as a coupon book.
options.viewport: A coupon book where each leg tears off: scan, sort, hand over.
options.case: The status grammar fits, but Dombivli households don't recognise airline ephemera, and it reads as travel.
options.risk: Foreign to the audience. Reads as a travel product.
options.kept: Nothing disappears, it gets stamped: statuses stamp onto the chit.

options.label: Emission Line Rail
options.thesis: Every item is a line on one calibrated rail.
options.viewport: A dark rail with item ticks, and the open item blooming above.
options.case: Dark, abstract and scientific. It contradicts the pinned white and green, and households wouldn't see themselves in it.
options.risk: Abstract and cold for a household tool.
options.kept: Certainty shown by shape, not colour.

options.label: Punched Brocade
options.thesis: Every recommendation woven from traceable instructions.
options.viewport: A woven motif with instruction rows beneath it.
options.case: A luxury-textile register that's wrong for waste. Only textile waste would connect with it.
options.kept: Every chit line traces back to its source document.

options.label: Broadcast Signal
options.lineage: TV test cards and alert crawls
options.thesis: Every page as a broadcast card with a warning crawl.
options.viewport: An alert card with a crawl pinned to the foot.
options.case: Alarmist and dark. It would make every page feel like an emergency.
options.risk: Creates anxiety and ignores the brief's palette.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.thesis: The assistant as a scrolling transcript.
options.viewport: One green transcript with a blinking cursor.
options.case: A developer costume. Households would read it as hacking, not help.
options.kept: The AI's checks print themselves as lines.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.viewport: A force diagram column with annotated nodes.
options.case: No link to waste or households beyond the idea of 'balance'.
options.risk: Abstract metaphor with nothing to act on.
options.kept: Distinct states that don't depend on hover.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean sustainability web app, done to a high standard.
canonCard.viewport: Centred headline and two buttons over a row of category cards, then How It Works.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every eco app by design.
